title: How to stay out of trouble
translation: If you want to stay out of trouble, here's how. Be sincere about everything. Be polite to everyone, whoever they are. And don't talk much.
That's good in anyone, men and women, young and old. But when someone young and good-looking speaks nicely, it stays with you. You can't help liking them.
Every kind of trouble starts the same way: you act too much at home, you play the expert, you look as if you own the place, and you treat other people as if they don't count.
original: {万|よろづ}の{科|とが}あらじと{思|おも}はば、{何事|なにごと}にも{誠|まこと}ありて、{人|ひと}を{分|わ}かず{恭|うやうや}しく、{言葉|ことば}すくなからむには{如|し}かじ。
{男女|なんによ}{老少|らうせう}みなさる{人|ひと}こそよけれども、{殊|こと}に{若|わか}くかたちよき{人|ひと}の、{言|こと}うるはしきは、{忘|わす}れがたく{思|おも}ひつかるるものなり。
よろづのとがは、{馴|な}れたるさまに{上手|じやうず}めき、{所|ところ}{得|え}たるけしきして、{人|ひと}をないがしろにするにあり。
literal: If you think you would like to have no faults at all, nothing beats being sincere in everything, respectful to people without distinction, and having few words.
Men and women, old and young, all such people are good, but especially when a young and good-looking person's speech is graceful, one comes to think of them unforgettably and is drawn to them.
All faults lie in acting familiar, playing the expert, looking as if one has found one's place, and slighting people.

notes.quote: 万の科あらじと思はば
notes.text: {科|とが}: 'fault, blame', something others can hold against you (the 1925 edition: 過失, 'mistake'). The edition gives the reading とが; later in the section the same word is written in kana.
'Without sorting people': treating high and low alike (the 1925 edition: 'without making distinctions between people').

notes.quote: 言葉すくなからむには如かじ
notes.text: には{如|し}かじ: 'nothing will be better than'. Talking little is a favourite point of Kenkō's; the good companion of section 1 also 'doesn't go on too long'.

notes.quote: さる人こそよけれども
notes.text: こそ … けれども: こそ takes the realis form よけれ, and ども turns it into 'but'. 'Such people are good, all of them, but…'
{思|おも}ひつく: 'to become attached to, to take a liking to'. る is spontaneous: it happens by itself (the 1925 edition: 'they leave an impression').
めく: 'to look like, to act like'. {上手|じやうず}めく: 'to put on the air of an expert' (the 1925 edition: 'showing off one's skill, acting skilled').
{所|ところ}{得|う}: 'to find one's place', and so 'to be in one's element, to look smug'. Compare {所得顔|ところえがほ} in section 235. ないがしろ, 'slighting', is still a modern word.
